questions.learningObjective: evaluate crop marks in a design critique
questions.stem: On Crop marks: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that a printer needs to know exactly where to cut the printed sheet. Which marks communicate this information?

options.text: Registration marks used only for aligning the color separations
options.misconception: confuses cutting guides with alignment guides

options.text: Fold marks that indicate where a sheet should be creased
options.misconception: names a different finishing instruction altogether

options.text: Crop marks placed at the corners of the finished size
Color bars that show the density of each printing ink
options.misconception: mistakes control strips for guides that indicate cutting

questions.explanation: Crop marks, also called trim marks, are short lines at the corners that show where the finished piece should be cut. They differ from registration marks, which align color separations, and from fold marks, which indicate where to crease.
questions.hint: Which corner marks tell the cutter exactly where the final edge falls?
